derived_from.hypothesis: The existing log cases assert that an append is proposed, that it carries the pinned date, and that it captures the substance — but nothing asserts the shape of the entry itself. The log-entry style contract in chat_prompt.md is specific: one bullet, one line, at most 160 characters, bracketed lowercase tokens of one to three words, an optional prose tail after an em dash, user-given numbers verbatim, and no recap of metrics the database already holds. That format is what makes log.md cheap to replay into every later prompt; a model that writes a paragraph, capitalises tokens, or restates HRV and sleep numbers degrades every downstream call while still looking like it did the right thing. This case guards the format so a model swap cannot quietly lose it. The scenario deliberately avoids proper nouns: the lowercase-token rule has never been ruled on for names, and a case should not be where an undecided question gets settled by accident.
convention_examples: - 2026-08-04 [run cut short] [walk run hybrid] — stopped at 3k feeling wrecked, then mixed walk/run with friend on bike
- 2026-08-01 [tempo drought broken] [sleep debt] — middle 2k @ 5:13/km inside 6k run; first clean tempo since W21

intent: A log append must follow the log-entry style contract and, above all, stand on its own: log.md is replayed into later prompts without the conversation that produced it, so an entry that only makes sense alongside today's message is worthless the moment it is read back.

judge_assertions.name: entry_stands_alone_without_the_conversation
judge_assertions.statement: Reading only the proposed log entry line, with no access to the conversation that produced it, a coach could tell what happened that day and why it mattered. The bracketed tokens name concepts carrying their own context — 'sleep short travel' rather than a bare 'tired' or 'poor', which would be meaningless on replay — and any prose tail after the em dash adds nuance the tokens cannot hold rather than restating them.

notes: Guards the log-entry style contract in chat_prompt.md, which the three existing log cases leave untested — they assert that an append happens, is dated, and captures the substance, but not its shape. Convention examples in derived_from are real entries from the operator's log.md. Deliberately covers the cheap-model path: log formatting is a compact, well-specified task that a flash-tier model handles well, so this case is what would catch a regression if that routing changes.
